usageNotes: Use this to inventory physical and virtual block devices visible to a specific node — useful before adding disks to Ceph, ZFS, or LVM storage. SMART health data is queried per disk by default, which can slow the response on nodes with many drives; pass skipsmart=true for faster enumeration when health status is not needed. Requires Sys.Audit on / or on /nodes/{node}.

examples.summary: List all unused disks on node pve1, skipping SMART checks for speed

tips: Set type=unused to quickly find unpartitioned disks eligible for new storage pools or Ceph OSDs.
Set type=journal_disks to find disks designated as Ceph journal/WAL/DB devices.
include-partitions=true is needed to see individual partitions alongside whole disks; partition entries include a 'parent' field pointing to the containing disk.
The 'osdid' and 'osdid-list' fields identify Ceph OSDs residing on that disk — a non-negative osdid means the disk is already claimed by Ceph.
SMART health is returned in the 'health' field (e.g. PASSED, FAILED); absent or empty health usually means the disk type does not support SMART.
